name: ChecklistDek
author: ashiquzzaman

sections.description:
ChecklistDek is the ultimate self-hosted WordPress agency hub for teams who manage multiple client sites. Whether you run launches and migrations, security hardening, monthly maintenance, or client onboarding, ChecklistDek helps you turn SOPs into structured checklists clients complete inside their own wp-admin—with audit-friendly history on infrastructure you control.

Stop juggling scattered docs, spreadsheets, and generic project tools that never show progress where clients actually work. With ChecklistDek, checklists and run history live on your own WordPress hub site. You connect remote properties with Application Passwords, deploy the bundled must-use client checklist panel on each managed site (one-time setup per site), and push runs so steps, notes, and wp-admin deep links stay in sync—without moving operations into a separate SaaS product.

Built for Repeatable Operations, Designed for Client Visibility: ChecklistDek features a three-column checklist builder with live client-panel preview, built-in template stacks, and core REST API automation for hub-side steps—with exclude-options so sensitive /wp/v2/settings fields never leave your guardrails. The dashboard tracks connection health, batch execution, drift checks, and a filterable activity log. Clients see the active checklist in wp-admin through the lightweight client panel, not email threads or exported PDFs alone.

Why Choose a Self-Hosted Agency Checklist Hub?

  • Own Your SOPs and Run Data: Keep sites, checklists, runs, and audit logs in your WordPress database on the hub. The Community build does not phone home to ChecklistDek analytics.
  • Clients Work Where They Already Are: Manual steps, optional notes, screenshots, and deep links surface in client wp-admin via the bundled mu-plugin panel—no separate client portal required.
  • Core REST Only for API Steps: Checklist automation uses WordPress Application Passwords and core REST endpoints on remote sites—not arbitrary remote code execution.
  • Hub Orchestration, Client Completion: Start and track runs from the hub; client completions sync back with per-run tokens. Failed hub↔client sync surfaces on the dashboard and in the live log feed.
  • Team-Ready Access Controls: Map ChecklistDek capabilities to WordPress roles, use agency presets (Admin, Developer, Auditor), and optionally encrypt Application Passwords stored on the hub.

How It Works

  1. Install on Your Hub: Activate ChecklistDek on your command-center WordPress site (6.2+). Complete the onboarding wizard to paste an SOP, pick a template, or start blank.
  2. Connect Client Sites: Register each site under ChecklistDek → Sites with an Application Password. Tag sites, test connection health, and optionally sync inventory from MainWP or WP Umbrella.
  3. Deploy the Client Panel: Upload the bundled client checklist panel to wp-content/mu-plugins/ on every managed site (Community: manual ZIP download; Pro may auto-deploy when licensed).
  4. Build and Push a Run: Create or clone a checklist, start a run from the dashboard, Sites, or Batch Run, and push the snapshot to the client panel. Progress, API steps, manual completions, and notes sync through the hub.
  5. Verify and Audit: Use drift monitor for baseline checks, filter Activity Logs by site and status, and review expandable detail fields when you need a full paper trail.

Designed for Every Agency Workflow

  • For Launch and Migration Teams: Use built-in launch, migration, and go-live templates; push runs site-by-site or queue the same checklist across many properties.
  • For Security and Maintenance Retainers: Run hardening, backup, and monthly maintenance stacks with manual client sign-off steps and hub-side API checks where appropriate.
  • For Freelancers and Small Agencies: Unlimited connected sites on Community; quick launch from the dashboard and expandable run history per site row.
  • For Operations Leads: Batch Run wizard, drift monitor, and role matrix so developers execute while auditors retain log visibility.
  • For Integrations-First Shops: Optional MainWP and WP Umbrella connectors import site lists and telemetry mapping rules—you still connect credentials and panels per site in ChecklistDek.

Comprehensive Checklist & Operations Toolkit

Build and operate checklists with dedicated hub screens and REST-driven admin UI:

  • Checklists → Templates: Browse built-in stacks by category, search across titles and steps, preview steps, and clone with Use Checklist. Community ships 17 templates in four categories; Pro expands the full library.
  • My Checklists Builder: Three-column canvas—drag-and-drop steps, per-step type (manual or API), deep-link inference, role mapping, note and screenshot toggles, and live client-panel preview.
  • Sites Registry: Connection health dots, client panel badge, tags and custom groups, push checklist modal, and nested run history without leaving the list.
  • Batch Run: Run Checklist wizard, multi-site batch queue, and drift monitor for permalink, visibility, and environment baselines (scheduled drift on Pro when licensed).
  • Activity Logs: Paginated audit table with summaries, View details, and raw payload inspection for support and compliance reviews.
  • Settings: Global enable switch, Application Password encryption, exclude-options for remote settings API payloads, client panel layout and title (three layouts on Community), and Access & Roles matrix.

Why Agencies Choose ChecklistDek

  • Replace Static SOPs with Living Checklists: Import JSON, clone templates, or paste text in onboarding—then edit in the visual builder with export for backups.
  • One Hub, Many Client Sites: Register unlimited sites on Community; track health, versions, and last errors from a single dashboard.
  • Client-Visible Progress: Push runs so stakeholders see step status, instructions, and admin deep links in their own dashboard.
  • Audit Without Spreadsheets: Immutable-style activity log with site, run, and step context; dashboard feed for at-a-glance operations.
  • Optional Connectors, No Lock-In: MainWP and WP Umbrella sync are user-initiated; manual Application Password registration always works.
  • Upgrade Path When You Grow: Pro and Agency packages add vault templates, auto-capture, notifications, scheduled drift, and hub panel auto-deploy—without rebuilding your hub database.

Community vs Pro Features

Community Version Features (this WordPress.org build):

  • Unlimited connected hub sites
  • Custom checklists with import/export JSON
  • 17 built-in templates in four categories (security, maintenance, performance, ecommerce)
  • Three client panel layout choices in Settings
  • Manual client panel upload via hub download ZIP and Retry panel install verification
  • Sites registry with tags, groups, connection tests, and expandable run history
  • Dashboard stats, connection ticker, live log feed, and quick launch
  • Batch Run (single-site wizard and multi-site queue) and manual drift verify
  • Activity Logs with filters and detail expansion
  • MainWP and WP Umbrella integrations (user-initiated sync)
  • Role capabilities, optional Application Password encryption on the hub
  • Onboarding wizard and template picker on dashboard and checklists

ChecklistDek Pro and Agency Features:

  • Full built-in template library (86 stacks across all categories)
  • Private Agency Vault (reusable team checklist templates—not Application Password storage)
  • Auto-Capture of client wp-admin actions into checklist steps
  • Email notifications and Slack, Discord, or Teams webhooks (opt-in events)
  • Scheduled drift verification cron
  • Hub auto-deploy of the client panel and MainWP Push Client Panel when licensed
  • Nine client panel layout choices

Supercharge Your Agency Workflow with ChecklistDek Pro

Community ChecklistDek is a complete hub for unlimited sites, custom checklists, batch runs, integrations, activity logs, and manual drift checks. ChecklistDek Pro is built for agencies that want faster panel rollout, richer template libraries, client-side capture, and proactive alerts—still on your own WordPress infrastructure.

  • Roll out panels faster: Auto-deploy the mu-plugin bundle from the hub when credentials allow, instead of manual ZIP uploads on every site.
  • Standardize intellectual property: Save private vault templates your team reuses across clients without mixing them into the public template grid.
  • Record how work really happens: Auto-Capture turns client admin actions into draft steps during a session you start.
  • Stay informed: Email and webhook notifications fire only for events you enable; drift alerts focus on newly detected configuration drift.
  • Upgrade without rebuilding: Install the Pro package on your hub (replacing this WordPress.org build), activate your license, and keep existing sites, checklists, and runs in the database.

Learn more and compare plans: Upgrade to ChecklistDek Pro

More Notable Products From the Author

ChecklistDek is developed by Asphalt Themes. If you build stores or personal brands on WordPress, these products from the same author may help:

  • Trustbadg – Trust Badges, Payment Icons & Secure Checkout Seals — Native Gutenberg trust badges and payment icons for WooCommerce and other e-commerce plugins, with automatic placements and inline SVG output.
  • Rezicraft – Professional Resume & CV Builder — Gutenberg-friendly online resumes with sections for experience, skills, and templates for job seekers.
  • Resumee — A WordPress resume and portfolio theme with flexible sections and SEO-friendly markup for professional profiles.

Why ChecklistDek vs. Generic Project Management SaaS

Checklist and ops tools built outside WordPress often force duplicate site lists, hide client progress behind portals clients never open, or charge per seat for audit history. ChecklistDek keeps the hub on WordPress, executes API steps through core REST, and shows live checklists in client wp-admin via a small mu-plugin—so launches and maintenance stay tied to the sites you already manage.

  • Data stays on your hub: Sites, checklists, runs, and logs remain in your database—not a vendor’s multi-tenant cloud.
  • No proprietary client portal: The client panel is standard wp-admin UI with your branding settings (panel title and layout).
  • WordPress-native permissions: Capability matrix aligns with how your agency already roles staff in wp-admin.
  • Transparent outbound traffic: Remote calls go only to sites you register and connectors you configure (see FAQ and External services).

Privacy

The Community build does not send checklist content, runs, or audit data to ChecklistDek-operated analytics servers. Outbound traffic is limited to user-registered remote WordPress sites (Application Password REST), checklist run snapshots after you install the client panel and push a run, and user-initiated integration sync when configured. Application Passwords may be encrypted at rest on the hub when enabled; decrypted credentials are not exposed in REST responses or audit views shown to non-privileged users. Pro webhook and email features (separate package) use only URLs and recipients you configure.

Performance

ChecklistDek is built for operational clarity without loading heavy UI on every admin request:

  • Dashboard stats, connection health, sites lists, and the live log feed use a cached dashboard payload invalidated when underlying data changes—so first paint on the hub dashboard stays fast.
  • Sites run history and full Activity Logs pagination use admin-ajax on expand or filter—not on every page load.
  • Built-in template sync on the hub runs in admin, REST, cron, and ajax contexts—not on public front-end requests after the initial seed.
  • Client panel CSS and JS load on remote sites only when an active run snapshot exists and the logged-in user may view the panel.

Use the onboarding wizard after activation to connect a site, install the client panel, and push your first run.

External services

Optional connectors run only when an administrator with Manage Settings starts an action under ChecklistDek → Integrations—not on activation or routine admin loads. ChecklistDek does not send checklists, runs, audit logs, or Application Passwords to these vendors.

MainWP Dashboard

MainWP (Dashboard on hub, Child on client sites) is optional and requires MainWP Dashboard on the hub.

When: Sync Sites, Preview Sync, or Push Client Panel in Integrations.

Data: Sync reads local MainWP tables on the hub (child ID, name, URL, optional versions) into ChecklistDek sites. Pro/Agency panel push may use MainWP Connect over HTTPS (child may fetch a bootstrap ZIP from your hub). Community does not use that install path—upload the client panel manually.

Why: Import your MainWP site list and optional field mapping; Pro/Agency may deploy the client panel without hub Application Passwords.

Legal: Terms of Service · Privacy Policy.

WP Umbrella Public API

WP Umbrella is optional. The connector calls https://public-api.wp-umbrella.com (for example GET /projects with your Public API token).

When: After you save a token or click Sync Sites / Preview Sync. Panel push uses Application Passwords to your sites only—not WP Umbrella.

Data: Project name, URL, ID, and optional version hints are stored locally; the token is encrypted on the hub and never shown in REST or UI. Token save may run a one-project validation request.

Why: Import WP Umbrella inventory and map fields before you connect sites in ChecklistDek.

Legal: Terms · Privacy Policy.
sections.installation:
Quick WordPress Installation (hub site)

  1. In your WordPress admin dashboard, navigate to Plugins → Add New.
  2. Search for ChecklistDek.
  3. Click Install Now, then click Activate.
  4. Complete the onboarding wizard or open ChecklistDek in the admin sidebar to connect your first client site and deploy the client checklist panel.

Manual Installation (hub site)

  1. Download the plugin archive and upload the checklistdek folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory on your hub server.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to ChecklistDek → Sites, register each client site with an Application Password, and complete client panel setup on every remote site before pushing checklists.

Client site setup (every managed site)

ChecklistDek checklists appear in client wp-admin only through the bundled must-use panel:

  1. Connect the site on ChecklistDek → Sites with an Application Password.
  2. Download checklistdek-client.php from the panel setup section in the site editor and upload the full client panel bundle to wp-content/mu-plugins/ on the client site.
  3. Click Retry panel install on the hub to verify the panel is detected.
  4. Push a checklist run from the hub; the client panel displays the active run snapshot.
sections.faq:
Who is ChecklistDek built for?

ChecklistDek is built for WordPress agencies, freelancers, and in-house web teams who manage multiple client sites and want repeatable checklists, client-visible progress in wp-admin, and audit-friendly history—without moving SOPs into a separate SaaS product.

Does ChecklistDek require a plugin on remote client sites?

Yes. Every managed remote site must have ChecklistDek’s bundled must-use client checklist panel in wp-content/mu-plugins/ (one-time setup per site). That panel is how checklists appear, how manual steps are completed, and how notes and progress sync with your hub. There is no supported “hub only, no client UI” workflow.

How do I install the client checklist panel on a remote site?

  1. Connect the site on ChecklistDek → Sites with an Application Password.
  2. Download checklistdek-client.php from the panel setup block in the site editor (or onboarding / connection tester).
  3. Upload it to wp-content/mu-plugins/ on the client site (create the folder if needed).
  4. Click Retry panel install on the hub to verify the connection.

The WordPress.org Community build does not write panel PHP into mu-plugins or uploads automatically—you install the bundled files yourself. The client panel ships with ChecklistDek; it is not a separate WordPress.org plugin listing.

Can I skip the must-use plugin and still show checklists to clients?

No. Email, exports, or hub-side tracking alone are not substitutes for the in-dashboard checklist experience ChecklistDek delivers through the client panel.

Does ChecklistDek work without MainWP or WP Umbrella?

Yes. Integrations are optional. You can register sites manually with Application Passwords, deploy the client panel, and run checklists without any connector plugin.

What is the difference between Community, Pro, and Agency?

Community (this WordPress.org plugin) is complete for its scope: unlimited hub sites, custom checklists, batch runs, integrations, Activity Logs, manual drift verification, 17 built-in templates in four categories, and three client panel layout choices in Settings. Client sites use the bundled mu-plugin you upload manually (this build does not auto-write panel files to remote servers).

Pro and Agency are separate downloads from Asphalt Themes with a larger template library, Private Agency Vault, Auto-Capture, email and webhook notifications, scheduled drift cron, hub auto-deploy of the client panel, nine panel layout choices, and licensed site tiers on paid plans. Application Password encryption in Settings is included in Community and Pro. They replace this plugin on your hub; your existing sites and checklists stay in the database.

Are credentials stored securely?

When enabled under Settings → Application password encryption, site Application Passwords are encrypted at rest using your WordPress salt keys. Decrypted passwords are never exposed in REST responses or audit entries shown to non-privileged users.

Is “Application password encryption” the same as Private Agency Vault?

No. Application password encryption (Settings, included in Community and Pro) protects Application Passwords stored on your hub for remote site connections. Private Agency Vault is a Pro feature for saving your own checklists as reusable team templates on the Checklists → Templates tab—it does not store site passwords.

What outbound connections does ChecklistDek make?

  • User-registered remote WordPress sites (Application Password REST calls)
  • Checklist run snapshots synced to registered sites after you install the client panel and push a run (Community uses manual panel upload; Pro/Agency may also auto-deploy panel files from the hub)
  • User-initiated integration sync (MainWP child sites or WP Umbrella Public API when configured)
  • Pro and Agency only: user-configured webhook URLs (Slack, Discord, Teams) and optional email alerts via WordPress wp_mail when those events are enabled in the separate paid package

Does ChecklistDek require WooCommerce on client sites?

No. WooCommerce-specific steps appear in some built-in templates, but the hub and client panel work with any WordPress 6.0+ site that supports Application Passwords and REST.

Can I use ChecklistDek on a local hub (MAMP, Local, etc.)?

Yes. The hub can manage local and remote URLs. The remote client may require the ?rest_route= fallback when pretty permalinks are broken; ChecklistDek handles that automatically for REST calls. Admin-ajax handlers are used for some heavy lists on memory-constrained local installs.

What happens when I uninstall ChecklistDek from the hub?

Uninstall removes ChecklistDek tables, options, and custom capabilities from the hub site. Client sites retain the mu-plugin files until you remove them manually from wp-content/mu-plugins/. Completed hub run history is deleted with the plugin—export checklists first if you need archives.

How do I upgrade to Pro or Agency?

Purchase from Asphalt Themes, install the Pro or Agency plugin package on your hub (replacing this WordPress.org build), and complete license activation in that package. Your existing sites and checklists remain in the database.
sections.changelog:
1.0.9

  • WordPress.org: expanded plugin description, FAQ, installation guidance, and external services documentation for directory review.
  • WordPress.org: add admin UI screenshots for the plugin listing.
  • Client checklist panel: bundled mu-plugin version 1.0.10.

1.0.8

  • Dashboard: surface hub↔client checklist sync failures in a dashboard error notice and Live Log Feed when the client marks a step but the hub does not update, or the hub updates but the client panel does not refresh.
  • Client panel hub callbacks: retry plain-permalink rest_route URLs and reject bogus HTTP 200 responses so step completions cannot silently fail when the hub is unreachable or misconfigured.
  • Batch Run: poll the active run while you watch step 3 so client-side completions update progress without a manual page reload.
  • Hub run start and push: verify the client checklist panel on each push and show “Client checklist panel is installed and ready” with push success; failed or unverified pushes surface an error instead of “run started” alone.
  • Fix fatal error on panel local install when wp_str_ends_with() is unavailable (replaced with PHP-compatible path suffix check).
  • Fix admin lockout after saving Access & Roles: WordPress menu checks now honor the role permission matrix and site administrators (manage_options).
  • Avoid plugin load fatals when the Freemius SDK is missing from a dev checkout (plugin no longer auto-pauses on require).
  • Client panel setup: download from onboarding or Sites now streams a full mu-plugin ZIP via admin-ajax so browsers save the file reliably (Community manual install).
  • Edition split: WordPress.org zip ships only working Community features (Pro PHP omitted at build time); Pro zip bundles premium modules and Freemius license gates.
  • WordPress.org zip omits all Private Agency Vault PHP, UI, and REST code; shared installer/build helpers no longer reference vault schema or license gates.
  • Checklists Templates tab: checklistdek_checklists_after_builtin_templates hook lets Pro inject Private Agency Vault UI without vault markup in the free package.
  • Private Agency Vault, Auto-Capture, notifications, scheduled drift, and hub panel auto-deploy are unavailable on Community (no in-plugin Pro upsell or disabled controls).
  • Pro hubs drop the legacy is_vault checklist column when Agency Vault is unavailable (cleanup omitted from WordPress.org zip).
  • WordPress.org Community: sidebar Upgrade redirects to the public pricing URL; legacy billing admin URLs redirect the same way (Pro zip shows Upgrade only when Freemius reports no premium license).

1.0.7

  • Settings: rename “Credential Vault Security” to “Application password encryption” and clarify it is separate from Private Agency Vault (team checklist templates).
  • Database 1.8.0: is_vault checklist column for Private Agency Vault.
  • Community: Pro-only UI omitted from Settings and Checklists where features are not bundled; org zip excludes Pro licensing PHP.

1.0.6

  • Sites: per-site Push Checklist, cached connection health, and unreachable-site warnings.
  • Dashboard: unify live log feed copy in audit format_row(); legacy cached feed rows backfill show_site_label only.
  • Community: removed in-plugin Billing page; Upgrade submenu opens the public ChecklistDek pricing page on asphaltthemes.com.

  • Sites run history and full Activity Logs pagination use admin-ajax on expand or filter—not on every page load.
  • Built-in template sync on the hub runs in admin, REST, cron, and ajax contexts—not on public front-end requests after the initial seed.
  • Client panel CSS and JS load on remote sites only when an active run snapshot exists and the logged-in user may view the panel.

Use the onboarding wizard after activation to connect a site, install the client panel, and push your first run.

External services

Optional connectors run only when an administrator with Manage Settings starts an action under ChecklistDek → Integrations—not on activation or routine admin loads. ChecklistDek does not send checklists, runs, audit logs, or Application Passwords to these vendors.

MainWP Dashboard

MainWP (Dashboard on hub, Child on client sites) is optional and requires MainWP Dashboard on the hub.

When: Sync Sites, Preview Sync, or Push Client Panel in Integrations.

Data: Sync reads local MainWP tables on the hub (child ID, name, URL, optional versions) into ChecklistDek sites. Pro/Agency panel push may use MainWP Connect over HTTPS (child may fetch a bootstrap ZIP from your hub). Community does not use that install path—upload the client panel manually.

Why: Import your MainWP site list and optional field mapping; Pro/Agency may deploy the client panel without hub Application Passwords.

Legal: Terms of Service · Privacy Policy.

WP Umbrella Public API

WP Umbrella is optional. The connector calls https://public-api.wp-umbrella.com (for example GET /projects with your Public API token).

When: After you save a token or click Sync Sites / Preview Sync. Panel push uses Application Passwords to your sites only—not WP Umbrella.

Data: Project name, URL, ID, and optional version hints are stored locally; the token is encrypted on the hub and never shown in REST or UI. Token save may run a one-project validation request.

Why: Import WP Umbrella inventory and map fields before you connect sites in ChecklistDek.
